source_text: Convenienter igitur Angelus sanctae Mariae virgini, primo omnium, illud, Ave gratia plena, Dominus tecum, praesignificavit: quoniam cum ipsa totus gratiae thesaurus reconditus erat. Ex omnibus enim generationibus, haec sola virgo, sancta corpore et spiritu extitit; solaque fert eum, qui verbo omnia portat. Et non solum admirationem nobis parit, sanctissimae illius in corpore pulchritudo; sed et virtutes animae eius.
orientation: The preacher goes on to explain why Gabriel greeted Mary as he did.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore fittingly the Angel signified beforehand to holy Mary the virgin, before all things, that word, Hail full of grace, The Lord with you: because with her the whole treasure of grace had been stored away. For out of all generations this virgin alone stood forth holy in body and in spirit; and she alone bears him who by his word bears all things. And not only does the beauty in body of that most holy woman bring forth wonder for us; but also the excellences of her soul bring forth wonder for us.

lemmas.gloss: bears, carries, here carries in womb

choices.why: Brief glossary fixes gratia plena as full of grace and bans favored one forms.
No verb in source, so keep verbless accompaniment rather than supplying is.

choices.english: the whole treasure of grace had been stored away
choices.why: totus is whole and reconditus erat is pluperfect passive, stored with her.
rejected: all the treasure of grace was hidden

choices.english: who by his word bears all things
choices.why: verbo is instrumental means and portat is present active, distinct from fert for Mary.
rejected: who carries all by the word

pass_b_english: So it was fitting that the angel should address his foretelling first of all to the holy virgin Mary: “Hail, full of grace; the Lord with you” (Luke 1:28). For the whole treasure of grace had been stored away with her.

For out of all generations this virgin alone has stood forth holy in body and in spirit, and she alone bears him who by his word bears all things. Not only does the bodily beauty of this most holy one fill us with wonder, but the virtues of her soul do as well.

last_rejected.quote: the angel should address his foretelling first of all
last_rejected.source_quote: Angelus sanctae Mariae virgini, primo omnium, illud, Ave gratia plena, Dominus tecum, praesignificavit
last_rejected.why: Praesignificavit means pre-signified or prefigured those words, not addressed a foretelling.
last_rejected.fix: Fittingly, then, the angel first of all prefigured for the holy virgin Mary those words: "Hail, full of grace; the Lord with you."
last_rejected.ruling: Praesignificavit means foreshowed or foretold; "address his foretelling" idiomatically renders the verb and dative (Mariae virgini) within its normal range.
